purpose: Data-only real CLI acceptance probes under the existing cooperative profile.
execution: Driver selects one resolved absolute Python executable as the independently owned policy tool and passes literal argv [-c, pythonCode]. The transport remains the real selected dotnet installation.

substitutions.{{VERSION}}: Exact declared provider tool version; JSON/string escape before insertion.
substitutions.{{TARGET}}: One complete JSON-escaped Python string literal for the case target; substitute without extra quotes.

policyRequirements: Replace only the selected tool probe executable and arguments; preserve the provider tool association and all admission obligations.
Regenerate and verify independent raw policy digest with the existing public producer/parser.
Retain the real fixture catalog/archive and their exact digest joins.
harnessRequirements: Require known direct CLI terminal, EOF and harness cleanup.
Expected CLI nonzero is a negative business case, not failed namespace cleanup.
Reject outer timeout, cancellation, output-limit or namespace-kill as evidence of product handling.
Require original absent target remains absent and no published provenance; existing target bytes must stay unchanged if the case supplies one.

productionEvidence.knownNonzero: CatalogScaffoldEffects.invoke: catalog.commandFailed after known child settlement
productionEvidence.outputLimit: CatalogScaffoldLinux.reader stops useful work; snapshot emits catalog.outputLimit

cases.name: probe-nonzero-7
cases.notes: The real policy tool exits 7; the CLI reports its own failed operation with exit 1. This is not CLI exit 7 or namespace timeout.

cases.name: probe-per-stream-output-limit
cases.notes: Finite 1.1MB output exceeds the 1MiB stdout ceiling while remaining below the 2MiB phase ceiling. Reader overflow stops useful work; actual scheduling may expose outputLimit or workStopped first. Empty diagnostics and outer harness failures are not accepted.

cases.name: probe-output-limit
cases.notes: Finite 2.2MB output exceeds the 1MiB per-stream and 2MiB phase limits. Once aggregate output spends the phase budget, the already-paid fixed catalog.diagnosticLimit marker truthfully preserves refusal; earlier outputLimit or workStopped may remain. Empty diagnostics are not accepted. Outer harness output-limit or namespace termination cannot count as product refusal.

cases.name: probe-product-deadline
cases.notes: Use the admitted 30-second product preflight budget and an outer deadline exceeding product cleanup. The product deadline, not harness namespace termination, must stop this probe.

cases.name: probe-product-sigint
cases.pythonCode: import os, signal, time; os.kill(os.getppid(), signal.SIGINT); time.sleep(1)
cases.notes: The actual directly launched policy probe signals its original CLI parent. This exercises Console.CancelKeyPress and the product token; no second process controller or harness cancellation event is used.

cases.name: probe-unexpected-stderr
cases.pythonCode: import sys; print("{{VERSION}}"); print("unexpected fixture stderr", file=sys.stderr)
cases.notes: Stdout is the exact declared tool version plus newline; nonempty stderr differs from the explicitly accepted SDK workload warning.

cases.name: probe-wrong-version
cases.notes: Known exit 0, EOF on both streams and bounded stdout do not establish the declared tool version.

cases.name: probe-appearing-target
cases.pythonCode: from pathlib import Path; target = Path({{TARGET}}); target.mkdir(); (target / "keep.txt").write_text("appearing-target-fixture\n", encoding="utf-8"); print("{{VERSION}}")
cases.notes: The policy probe runs after createPrivateRoot checked target absence. It introduces one caller-owned target with known sentinel bytes. Require no-replace publication refusal and exact sentinel preservation, not equality to the initially absent snapshot. No second process controller or concurrent fixture thread is used.
